# feat(core): route numerical diagnostics through Python warnings module -->

## Related URLs

- Issues
  - Closes <https://github.com/connect0459/rustgression/issues/170>
- PRs
  - N/A

## [Required] Overview

Two numerical diagnostics in the Rust core wrote directly to stderr via `eprintln!`: a large SVD condition number warning emitted by TLS, and a subnormal-number detection emitted by the input validation layer (affecting both OLS and TLS). Because `eprintln!` bypasses Python's I/O layer entirely, callers had no way to suppress these messages, capture them in tests, or escalate them to exceptions — any filtering with `warnings.simplefilter` or `warnings.catch_warnings` had no effect, and the output surfaced as unavoidable noise even for computations whose results were numerically correct (e.g., small-scale TLS input with a large but finite condition number).

This PR routes both diagnostics through Python's `warnings` machinery.

**`NumericalWarning`**: A new `NumericalWarning` exception class (subclass of `UserWarning`) is defined and registered in the Python module. It serves as the category for all machine-precision-level advisories emitted by the library, giving callers a named filter target distinct from generic `UserWarning`.

**Large condition number (TLS)**: When the SVD condition number exceeds 10¹², the diagnostic is now emitted as a `NumericalWarning` via `warnings.warn()` rather than written to stderr. The message text and the threshold are unchanged; only the delivery mechanism changes.

**Subnormal number detection (OLS and TLS)**: When an input array element is nonzero but below `f64::MIN_POSITIVE` (i.e., a IEEE 754 subnormal), the advisory is now emitted as a `NumericalWarning` per element. The message text and the detection logic are unchanged.

Because `warnings.warn()` raises if the active filter for the category is `"error"`, the `emit_numerical_warning` helper propagates the resulting `PyResult::Err` back through the call stack — callers using `warnings.simplefilter("error", NumericalWarning)` will receive an exception instead of a silent continuation. All three warning behaviours — suppress, record, escalate — are verified by the new test suite.

`NumericalWarning` is exported from the package top-level so callers can reference it without reaching into the internal Rust extension module.

## [Required] Release

- Release date: Anytime
- Release considerations: This is a diagnostic delivery change with no change to point estimates, error conditions, or the API surface. The only observable behaviour change is that `eprintln!` output no longer appears on stderr; the same information now travels through the `warnings` module. Callers who previously detected the messages by capturing stderr will need to switch to `warnings.catch_warnings`. `NumericalWarning` is a new public symbol added to `__all__`.

## Post-Release Verification

- All 134 tests pass in both the Docker dev environment and the local Python environment.
- Rollback: Revert the branch.

Summary
Auxiliary OpenAI SDK clients (vision, title generation, etc.) now use the same env-only proxy policy as the main agent, so a macOS system proxy that drops the ExceptionsList no longer breaks `vision_analyze` against internal endpoints.

Root cause: aux clients were constructed with bare `OpenAI(...)`, leaving httpx `trust_env=True` to read `urllib.request.getproxies()` — which picks up the macOS system proxy (Clash/V2Ray) but ignores its exception list. Main agent chat already routed through an explicit keepalive transport with `HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` resolution; aux did not, so it diverged and failed with `SSL: UNEXPECTED_EOF_WHILE_READING`.

Salvaged from #53863 by @HexLab98 onto current `main` (cherry-picked, authorship preserved). Closes #53702.

## Changes
- `agent/process_bootstrap.py`: add module-level `build_keepalive_http_client()` — a faithful mirror of `AIAgent._build_keepalive_http_client` (custom httpx transport + explicit `HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` via `_get_proxy_for_base_url`), with async support.
- `agent/auxiliary_client.py`: route every aux `OpenAI(...)` construction through a `_create_openai_client()` wrapper that injects the env-only transport; threads through the sync→async conversion path so async vision is covered.
- `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client_proxy_env.py`: regression tests for env-proxy routing and the macOS `getproxies()` bypass.

## Why it works
A custom `transport=` disables httpx's `allow_env_proxies` (`trust_env and proxy is None and transport is None`), so the system proxy is never auto-applied — only the explicit `proxy=` argument governs routing, and `NO_PROXY` is still honored for internal/loopback hosts.

## Validation

|---|---|---|
| Before | proxied → SSL EOF | proxied (ok) |
| After | DIRECT, 0 proxy mounts | proxy mount intact |

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client_proxy_env.py` → 5/5 green
- Broader aux suite (`test_auxiliary_client`, `test_auxiliary_main_first`, `test_auxiliary_transport_autodetect`, `test_auxiliary_named_custom_providers`) → green
- E2E (real imports, HTTPS_PROXY + NO_PROXY set): internal host yields 0 proxy mounts (sync + async); external host keeps its proxy mount.

Summary

`LocalArtifactStore` accepted arbitrary path strings in `write()`, `read()`, and `delete()` without verifying they resolved within `_base`. A caller using the store directly (bypassing `WorkspaceManager`) could read, write, or delete files anywhere on the filesystem.

# Changes

- Added `_resolve_and_validate()` private method that resolves the path and raises `ValueError` if it escapes `self._base`
- Replaced ad-hoc branching in `read()` and `delete()` with a single call to `_resolve_and_validate()`
- In `write()`, validation now runs **before** `mkdir()` so no directories are created on traversal attempts

## Description
This Pull Request addresses **Issue #7** by designing and implementing a Custom Threat Rules Editor. Previously, regular expressions and keyword definitions were hardcoded, leaving administrators unable to add temporary rules (e.g., allowlisting safe internal senders, or blocklisting specific spam campaigns). 

This changes the system to support a rules engine that bypasses AI model inference entirely if custom allowlist/blocklist conditions are satisfied.

## Changes Made
1. **Added Custom Rules Manager (`models/custom_rules_manager.py`):**
   - Implemented logic to save and load custom rules from a persistent local configuration file (`custom_rules.json`).
   - Implemented checking functionality (`check_custom_rules`) to match inputs against allowlist (safe domain strings) and blocklist (regular expression patterns).
   - Exposed manager functions via `models/__init__.py`.
2. **Streamlit UI Editor Integration (`app.py`):**
   - Added a **"🛡️ Custom Threat Rules Editor"** section under the **Settings** page.
   - Built forms allowing administrators to add domains to the Allowlist or regex patterns to the Blocklist (with active regex compilation validation).
   - Handled list rendering and single-click removal (`🗑️`) of configured rules.
3. **Inference Bypass Logic (`app.py`):**
   - Integrated custom rule checks at the start of both Single Model and Ensemble predictions.
   - If a message matches a custom rule, it immediately resolves the label (`HAM` for allowlist, `SPAM` for blocklist) with `1.0` confidence and triggers threat categorization without loading models or performing AI model inference.
4. **Unit & Logic Testing (`tests/test_custom_rules.py`):**
   - Added comprehensive tests covering default rules generation, storage persistence, matching logic, regex safety, and allowlist priority over blocklist checks.

## Verification
- Ran all custom rules test suites (`python -m pytest tests/test_custom_rules.py`), which passed successfully.
- Verified that allowlist and blocklist rules persist across system restarts and correctly bypass ML model inference.

## What & why

Parent #1175 (bug-hunt round-2), finding #5 — LOW, latent. Per convention #569, every write must go through `execute_write`/`transaction` (they hold the connection-wide `_write_lock`, load-bearing under `isolation_level=None` + single shared connection). Three `ChannelsRepository` methods wrote through `self._database.db.execute(...)` **directly** in their `commit=False` branches, bypassing the lock:

- `set_filtered_bulk(commit=False)` — `channels.py:287`
- `reset_all_filters(commit=False)` — `channels.py:310`
- `reset_filters_for_pks(commit=False)` — `channels.py:333`

Safe today only because the lone runtime caller (`analyzer.apply_filters`, `analyzer.py:273-276`) wraps them in `Database.transaction()` — so the lock is held transitively. But the invariant was **unenforceable**: any future `commit=False` caller outside a transaction would silently reintroduce the #569 race.

## Fix

Chose the `assert self._database.db.in_transaction` option over the `conn=`-explicit alternative. Rationale:
- **Minimal & surgical** — matches the S / LOW scope. The `conn=` path is M-sized API churn (repo + facade + bundles + analyzer caller signatures).
- **Does not touch the `analyzer.py` caller** — it already runs inside `transaction()`, so the assert passes; no signature change.
- **Mirrors existing convention** — the file already guards with `assert self._database is not None`.
- `aiosqlite.Connection.in_transaction` reliably reflects an open `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` block under `isolation_level=None`.

## Tests (`tests/repositories/test_channels_repository.py`)

6 new tests — RED before the fix, GREEN after:
- 3 enforcement: `commit=False` **outside** a transaction → `AssertionError` (was: silently executed the write).
- 3 positive: `commit=False` **inside** `Database.transaction()` → works (proves the analyzer path is unbroken).

What

`POST /admin/fundamentals/refresh` — re-fetch SEC companyfacts + re-derive `financial_periods` for a named symbol cohort *now*, bypassing the `plan_refresh` watermark gate.

Body: `{"symbols": ["IEP","ET",...]}` (case-insensitive, ≤50 distinct). Auth: `require_session_or_service_token`.

## Why

The daily job only refreshes CIKs whose top-accession changed, so a `TRACKED_CONCEPTS`/allowlist extension never backfills existing instruments until SEC ships them a fresh filing (issue #677). This gives the operator a targeted trigger.

## Design

- **Single source of truth.** The resolve→fetch→normalize core (previously inline in `scripts/force_refresh_fundamentals.py`, #674) is extracted to `app/services/fundamentals/force_refresh.py::run_force_refresh`. Both the CLI and the new endpoint consume it — no drift. `resolve_symbols`/`ResolvedSymbol` re-exported from the script for back-compat (existing test unchanged).
- **Connection model.** Sync handler (FastAPI runs it in the threadpool — no event-loop block) on a dedicated `connect_job()` connection, **not** the pooled `get_conn` dependency: a 5-60s SEC fetch must not starve the request pool.
- **Commit discipline** (psycopg3 savepoint≠commit): commit between resolve / fetch / normalize phases so the per-instrument transactions inside `refresh_financial_facts`/`normalize_financial_periods` run top-level, not as savepoints under one multi-minute outer tx.
- **Per-symbol response contract.** Instrument-dedup applies to fetch/normalize *work* (`ForceRefreshResult.fetched`), not the *response* (`ForceRefreshResult.resolved`) — two tickers sharing one instrument both appear in `results`, work runs once.
- Data treatment unchanged from the daily path (settled "Fundamentals provider posture", #532); only the trigger is new.

## Security model

Endpoint gated by `require_session_or_service_token` (same gate as `/jobs/{name}/run`). No new auth surface. Resolver uses bound params (`UPPER(i.symbol) = ANY(%(symbols)s)`), no interpolation. Writes only `financial_facts_raw` + `financial_periods` via the existing reviewed ingest functions.

## Tests

- Pure, fast-tier: `tests/test_fundamentals_force_refresh_helpers.py` — `_distinct_symbols` (case/dedup/empty), `dedupe_resolved` (instrument-dedup, two-symbols-one-instrument, passthrough). 7 passed.
- DB-tier resolver coverage already exists (`tests/test_force_refresh_fundamentals.py`, imports unchanged via re-export).

## Codex

- ckpt-1 (spec): case-insensitive resolve + primary-listing winner, dedup requested, idempotent-normalize + concurrency documented.
- ckpt-2 (diff): caught the per-symbol-response-vs-work dedup conflation (fixed) + restored the CLI deduped-count log.

## Dev verification (commit 97fabe52)

| Clause | Result |
|---|---|
| Smoke panel `{AAPL,GME,MSFT,JPM,HD,aapl}` | `requested=5` (aapl deduped), `resolved=5`, `facts_upserted=33407`, `symbols_failed=0`, `periods_canonical_upserted=419` |
| Validation | empty→400, unauth→401 |
| Operator-visible figure | `/instruments/AAPL/financials` renders revenue **$111.184B** (Q2 FY2026, end 2026-03-28) from `financial_periods` |
| Cross-source | SEC companyconcept AAPL `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax` = **111,184,000,000** for 2025-12-28→2026-03-28 (10-Q FY2026 Q2) — exact match |

## Scope

Part A only. **Part B** (`expected_filings` table + `expected_filings_poller` job — event-driven filing-poll watchlist) deferred to **#1788**; needs a schema migration + scheduler lane.

Spec: `docs/specs/api/2026-06-28-fundamentals-force-refresh.md`.

Closes #677.

Summary
Telegram bot-authored messages are now filtered by the gateway authorization path instead of being treated as authorized human input.

Root cause: the Telegram adapter's `build_source()` call never populated `source.is_bot`, so the auth bot-filter (`authz_mixin.py`, `getattr(source, "is_bot", False)`) always saw `False`. A second Hermes profile on the same machine therefore accepted and echoed messages sent by the first profile's bot, producing duplicate replies.

## Changes
- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`: pass `is_bot=bool(getattr(user, "is_bot", False))` to `build_source()` so the PTB `User.is_bot` flag reaches the auth path.
- `gateway/authz_mixin.py`: add `Platform.TELEGRAM: "TELEGRAM_ALLOW_BOTS"` to `platform_allow_bots_map`, mirroring the existing `DISCORD_ALLOW_BOTS` / `FEISHU_ALLOW_BOTS` opt-in UX (`none` / `mentions` / `all`).
- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` (`_apply_yaml_config`): bridge `telegram.allow_bots` from `config.yaml` to the `TELEGRAM_ALLOW_BOTS` env var (env takes precedence), alongside the other telegram config keys.
- Tests: new `tests/gateway/test_telegram_bot_auth_bypass.py` (adapter propagation + real `_is_user_authorized` path), `test_config.py` bridge tests, and env-isolation additions to the Discord/Feishu bypass tests.

## Validation
| Condition | Auth filter decision |
|---|---|
| bot, no flag | BLOCKED (default secure) |
| bot, `TELEGRAM_ALLOW_BOTS=all` | ALLOWED |
| bot, `TELEGRAM_ALLOW_BOTS=none` | BLOCKED |
| human in allowlist | ALLOWED |

E2E-verified against the real `GatewayRunner._is_user_authorized` path with real imports. Targeted suite: 133 tests pass (telegram bot auth, group gating, callback fail-closed, config bridge), 0 failed.

Summary
A `custom_providers` config that names the model under `model.name` (or `model.model`) now resolves correctly instead of sending an empty `model=` to the backend. Fixes #34500.

**Root cause:** the chat-model id is read as `default or model` at ~14 independent sites (CLI, gateway, cron, curator, oneshot, fallback, profiles, …). None honored `name`. So `model: {name: <id>, provider: <custom>}` resolved to an empty string and the request went out with `model=` → HTTP 400 from OpenAI-compatible backends. Display paths (`hermes status` / `dump`) *already* read `model.name`, so they showed the model while the request silently failed — which is why this was hard to spot and attracted multiple partial fixes.

Rather than patch every reader (the whack-a-mole that left this open), the fix canonicalizes the model id at the **single load/save chokepoint**.

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/config.py` — `_normalize_root_model_keys()` now promotes `model.model` / `model.name` → `model.default` (precedence `default > model > name`) and drops the stale alias. Runs on both `load_config()` and `save_config()`, so config.yaml is migrated canonical on next write. Every present/future reader sees a populated `default`.
- `gateway/run.py` — `_load_gateway_config()` replays the same normalization (the gateway reads raw YAML and bypasses `load_config()`).
- `tests/cli/test_cli_init.py` — 7 regression tests (alias promotion, precedence, stale-alias drop, empty stays empty, save round-trip migration).

## Validation
| config | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `model: {name: X, provider: custom}` | request `model=` → 400 | `model=X` ✓ |
| `model: {model: X}` | aliased only at some sites | `model.default=X` everywhere ✓ |
| `model: {default: X, name: Y}` | — | `default=X`, stale `name` dropped ✓ |
| `model: {provider: custom}` | empty | stays empty (no fabricated id) ✓ |

E2E verified all four resolution paths (`load_config`, `runtime_provider._get_model_config`, `cli.py`, `_resolve_gateway_model`) return the model with the issue's exact repro config. Targeted suites green: `test_cli_init` (53), `test_runtime_provider_resolution` + `test_empty_model_fallback` (146), `test_config` (121), gateway config/model-recovery/managed-scope loaders (20).

Credit: root-cause analysis and fix direction from @Bartok9 (#34502, submitted first) and @v86861062 (#34527). This lands their insight at the single chokepoint instead of N call sites.

Summary
The `execute_code` sandbox keeps stripping Hermes provider credentials even when the provider blocklist can't be imported.

`tools/env_passthrough.py:_is_hermes_provider_credential()` returned `False` when `tools.environments.local` failed to import — fail-open. Because `_scrub_child_env()` lets env-passthrough vars bypass the secret-substring net (rule 1), a skill could declare a Hermes provider credential (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) in `required_environment_variables`, get it registered while the import was down, and have the operator's real key copied into the `execute_code` child. That reopens the GHSA-rhgp-j443-p4rf bypass.

## Changes
- `tools/env_passthrough.py`: on blocklist import failure, log and `return True` (treat the name as a protected provider credential and refuse passthrough) instead of `return False`.
- `tests/tools/test_env_passthrough.py`: regression test simulating the import failure across the full `register_env_passthrough` → `_scrub_child_env` path; also asserts the non-failure path (third-party `TENOR_API_KEY` still registerable) is unaffected.
- `scripts/release.py`: AUTHOR_MAP entry for the contributor.

## Validation
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Blocklist import fails, skill registers `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | registered → key leaks into child | refused → key absent from child |
| `PATH` in child env (import failure) | present | present |
| `TENOR_API_KEY` (blocklist available) | registerable | registerable |
| Targeted tests | — | 18/18 pass |
| E2E (real register + scrub under simulated import failure) | — | leak blocked, no regression |

Salvaged from #37951 by @coygeek (authorship preserved). Stripped the PR's hardcoded blocklist snapshot — `return True` already fails closed absolutely, and a mirrored copy of `_HERMES_PROVIDER_ENV_BLOCKLIST` would drift out of sync. Closes the cluster with #40228 and #38141. Fixes #37950.

Summary
The installer no longer hangs forever on "Build desktop app" (or the earlier dependency steps) when an npm/Electron download stalls — a stall now self-heals via the existing mirror fallback instead of hanging.

Root cause: `install_desktop()` ran `npm ci` / `npm run pack` with no wall-clock cap (and the sibling browser-tools / TUI dependency installs had the same gap). The pack step fetches the ~150 MB Electron binary from GitHub; on a throttled or region-blocked link that download *stalls* rather than fails — npm never errors and never exits. So the installer sat on step 9/11 "Build desktop app" indefinitely with only harmless `npm warn deprecated` lines visible. The merged self-heal escalation (cache purge → dist restore → npmmirror fallback, #42998/#47276/#48091) only fires when `pack` returns non-zero, so a *stall* bypassed it entirely.

## Changes
- `scripts/install.sh`: generalize `run_browser_install_with_timeout` into `run_with_timeout` — GNU `timeout` / `gtimeout` for external commands, else a pure-shell process-group watchdog (so stock macOS, where neither binary exists, is also protected). Shell functions (`_desktop_pack`) always take the pure-shell path (the `timeout` binary can't exec a function). The timeout is normalized to an integer, and a final boundary recheck avoids mislabeling a just-finished command as a timeout.
- Wrap the desktop `npm ci` / `npm install` and all three `_desktop_pack` attempts (`DESKTOP_BUILD_TIMEOUT`, default 900s).
- Wrap the sibling browser-tools and TUI registry `npm install`s (`NODE_DEPS_TIMEOUT`, default 600s) — same stall class, previously unprotected; dropped their `2>/dev/null` so a timeout is visible.
- All timeouts env-overridable (bootstrap-script constants, not `HERMES_*` runtime config — `install.sh` runs before any `config.yaml` exists).

## Validation
| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Electron/registry download stalls (trickles `npm warn`, never exits) | installer hangs forever | bounded non-zero exit → mirror self-heal |
| `timeout`/`gtimeout` present, external cmd | n/a | passthrough; timeout → 124 |
| stock macOS (no coreutils), stalled cmd | no protection (ran bare) | killed via process-group, 124, **no orphans** |
| function target (`_desktop_pack`) | n/a | runs via pure-shell, propagates exit code; **no env pollution** |
| command finishes in the final poll interval | n/a | returns its real exit code, not a false 124 |
| non-integer / empty timeout value | n/a | normalized to default, loop doesn't crash |

- Unit harness: 14/14 scenarios pass (external/function paths, binary + pure-shell, boundary recheck, integer guard, process-group kill with no orphans, no `BASH_FUNC_` env leak).
- E2E: drove `install_desktop` with a mocked npm that prints deprecation warnings then `sleep 60` — returned rc=1 in ~4s instead of hanging, emitted the mirror guidance, left no orphaned npm/sleep processes.
- `bash -n scripts/install.sh` passes.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
`scripts/install.ps1`'s `Install-Desktop` has the same no-timeout flow, but the Windows timeout mechanism uses different PowerShell primitives (`Wait-Process -Timeout` / jobs) and there's no reported Windows hang for this. Left as a separate change to keep this fix focused and testable on the reported platform (macOS).

Summary
Widens the force-exit backstop (#53107) so **every** gateway exit path is wedge-proof — including the three `raise SystemExit(code)` paths that the base fix left vulnerable.

The base fix (force-exit after graceful shutdown via `os._exit`, PR #53121 by @LeonSGP43) has already merged to `main`. It covers the boolean-return paths, but `start_gateway()` also raises `SystemExit(code)` on the clean-fatal-config (#51228), planned-restart, and service-restart paths — those still propagate to CPython interpreter finalization (`Py_FinalizeEx` joins all non-daemon threads), so a wedged `ThreadPoolExecutor` tool/LLM worker can still hang the process there. This PR closes that remaining gap.

## Changes
- `gateway/run.py`: `main()` now catches `SystemExit` from `asyncio.run(start_gateway(...))` and routes its code through the same `_exit_after_graceful_shutdown` / `os._exit` backstop (None→0, int→code, str→1).
- `gateway/run.py`: `_exit_after_graceful_shutdown` now **releases the PID file + runtime lock explicitly** before `os._exit`. `os._exit` bypasses `atexit`, and the early SystemExit paths (fatal-config / startup-aborted) raise right after `runner.start()` without going through `_stop_impl` — so they previously relied on `atexit` to release both. Doing it in the backstop makes it the single guaranteed cleanup chokepoint; both calls are idempotent (no-op on the normal `_stop_impl` path, actual cleanup on the early-exit paths).
- `tests/gateway/test_gateway_process_exit.py`: +4 tests on the merged base — terminates via `os._exit` not `SystemExit`; `SystemExit(78)`→`os._exit(78)`; `SystemExit(None)`→`os._exit(0)`; `SystemExit("msg")`→`os._exit(1)`; and a guard that the backstop releases the PID file + runtime lock.

## Validation
| Exit path | Before this PR | After |
|---|---|---|
| boolean return + wedged worker | force-exits (base fix) | force-exits |
| `raise SystemExit(code)` + wedged worker | hangs in `Py_FinalizeEx` (unprotected) | force-exits with carried code |
| early fatal-config exit + `os._exit` | (would leak PID file/lock — atexit skipped) | PID file + lock released in the backstop |

- 7 targeted tests pass; `ruff` clean; `py_compile` OK.
- E2E (real subprocess, wedged non-daemon worker): old `sys.exit`/`SystemExit` path hangs (killed at 6s, rc=124); boolean path exits 1s/code 1; SystemExit-routing path → `SystemExit(78)` caught → exits 0s/code 78.
- E2E (real PID file + runtime lock): `_exit_after_graceful_shutdown(78)` exits code 78 AND removes the PID file — leak on the early-exit paths confirmed closed.

## Credit
Builds on @LeonSGP43's now-merged base fix (#53121). The `os._exit-not-SystemExit` regression test is adapted from @AgenticSpark's duplicate PR #53122 — both contributors credited.

## Follow-up context
The module-name/frame identity is unrelated here; this PR is purely the exit-path widening + the associated cleanup guarantee.

Closes #53107.

Summary
Config-backed `quick_commands` are now gated through the gateway's admin/user slash-access policy, closing an authorization bypass: a non-admin allowlisted gateway user could invoke admin-only quick commands — including `type: exec` shell commands that run in the gateway process — even when the operator set `allow_admin_from` / `user_allowed_commands` to lock them out.

Root cause: the early slash gate in `_handle_message` only fires for registry-known commands (`is_gateway_known_command(canonical)`). `quick_commands` are never in the gateway command registry, so they slipped straight past the gate to the `type: exec` dispatch sink unchecked.

Fixes #44727.

## Changes
- `gateway/run.py`: call `_check_slash_access(source, command)` at the `quick_commands` dispatch site (the single exec chokepoint, cold-path only), using the raw typed command name, before resolving/running `qcmd`.
- `tests/gateway/test_slash_access_dispatch.py`: 3 integration tests driving the real `_handle_message` — non-admin denied for an unlisted exec quick command (the PoC), admin runs it, non-admin runs it when it's in `user_allowed_commands`.

## Validation
Targeted suite: `tests/gateway/test_slash_access_dispatch.py` — 21/21 passing.

E2E against the real `GatewayRunner._handle_message`:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Non-admin (999), empty `user_allowed_commands` (the PoC) | ⛔ DENIED — bypass closed |
| Admin (111) | RUNS — admin unaffected |
| Non-admin (999), command in `user_allowed_commands` | RUNS — opt-in works |
| No policy set (`allow_admin_from` unset) | RUNS — backward-compat intact |

## Credit
Same fix independently submitted in #44791 (@maxpetrusenko, earliest) and #45536 (@zapabob). This salvage uses the sink-gate approach; both contributors co-authored.

Summary

`hermes gateway install` now works headlessly on Linux/systemd — non-TTY contexts (provisioning, CI, `ssh host 'hermes gateway install'`, `</dev/null`) install with sensible defaults instead of reading EOF and aborting with no service installed.

Root cause: PR #28874 (Windows idempotency) changed the *shared* systemd branch in `hermes_cli/gateway.py` to call `prompt_yes_no` unconditionally. The Windows branch honored `args.start_now`/`start_on_login`; the systemd branch ignored them and prompted every time. `prompt_yes_no` reads stdin and aborts on EOF, so any non-TTY invocation hung/failed.

Fixes #42065.

## Changes

- `hermes_cli/gateway.py`: systemd install branch honors `--start-now`/`--start-on-login` (mirrors the Windows path); when flags are absent it prompts only on a TTY, else falls back to `True` defaults. `systemd_install()` gained a `non_interactive` flag so the second hidden prompt — *"Remove the legacy unit(s) before installing?"* — is also bypassed in headless contexts.
- `hermes_cli/subcommands/gateway.py`: promoted the four `--start-*` flags from `argparse.SUPPRESS` to visible `--help` text.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway.py`: flag-bypass, non-TTY-defaults, and legacy-unit-skip coverage; existing `systemd_install` mocks accept the new kwarg.

## Validation

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `install </dev/null` (non-TTY) | hangs on EOF / exits ≠0, no unit | installs with defaults, starts, no prompt |
| `install` (TTY, no flags) | prompts ×2 | prompts ×2 (unchanged) |
| `install --no-start-now` | prompted anyway | flag honored, service not started |
| legacy units present, non-TTY | prompt could still hang | removed without prompting |

53/53 tests in `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway.py` pass. E2E-verified all four paths with a real non-TTY stdin and real `gateway_command()` calls.

## Credit

Salvage of @liuhao1024's PR #42071 (flag-honoring + non-TTY, submitted first) with @kyssta-exe's PR #42124 legacy-unit-prompt fix folded in. Both authorships preserved.

Summary
Removed/unauthorized Telegram users can no longer inject prompt content — the user-level auth gate now runs at intake, before any text/photo batching, `MessageEvent` construction, dispatch, or unmentioned-group observation.

Root cause: `_should_process_message` (group-mention/topic gating), `_build_message_event`, and batching all ran before the per-user allowlist (`_is_user_authorized` in `gateway/authz_mixin.py`) — which only fires in the runner. By the time the runner rejected the sender, the prompt had already entered the agent path. Worse, unmentioned group chatter from a removed user was persisted into the session transcript via `_observe_unmentioned_group_message`, leaking into the agent's observed context independent of dispatch.

Fixes #40863.

## Changes
- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`: new `_is_user_authorized_from_message()` + `_source_from_message_for_auth()` + `_telegram_auth_env_configured()`. Gate added to all four inbound handlers (`_handle_text_message`, `_handle_command`, `_handle_location_message`, `_handle_media_message`) — placed before `_should_process_message`/the observe branch so the transcript-observe path is gated too.
- Reuses the runner's `_is_user_authorized()` with a correctly-shaped `SessionSource` (dm / group / forum, real `chat_id` for `TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_*`), falls back to env allowlists, and only rejects when an allowlist actually exists — unknown DMs with no allowlist still reach the pairing flow. Channel posts authorize via `sender_chat` identity when `from_user` is absent.
- `tests/gateway/test_telegram_auth_check.py`: new (17 tests) — unauthorized blocked before event build, observe-context leak closed, channel posts pass user-level auth, group-allowlist source shaping, pairing-flow preservation.
- `scripts/release.py`: AUTHOR_MAP entry for cmcejas.

## Validation
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Removed DM user | event built + dispatched, then rejected | rejected at intake, no event built |
| Removed user, unmentioned group msg | text persisted to observed transcript | not observed |
| Authorized user | works | works |
| Unknown DM, no allowlist | reaches pairing | reaches pairing (preserved) |

- 17 new tests + 148 sibling Telegram tests (group-gating, channel-posts, documents, topic-mode, photo-interrupts, bot-auth-bypass) green — no bypasses needed.
- E2E (real adapter, isolated `HERMES_HOME`): all 4 scenarios above pass.

## Credit
Salvage of two independent fixes for #40863. liuhao1024 (#40916) submitted the earliest fix (early auth helper + channel-post `sender_chat` handling, folded in here); Carlos Manuel Cejas / cmcejas (#41188, the issue reporter) authored the implementation salvaged here, which additionally closes the observe-context leak and shapes the source for group allowlists. Both targeted the pre-extraction `gateway/platforms/telegram.py`; re-applied onto the current `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`. Authorship preserved via Co-authored-by trailers.

**Duplication and centralisation**
- **`_build_where`**: new `persistence/_shared/_filter_clauses.py` with one builder per `*FilterSpec`. All 10 filter types across both backends (20 sites) delegate, passing the backend's placeholder token (`?`/`%s`) and empty-filter fallback (`1=1`/`TRUE`). `evolution_outcome` keeps its raw-clause-list shape and takes serialisation callbacks for the SQLite-vs-Postgres bool/datetime handling; `deliverable_receipt` keeps its mandatory `project_id` seed. (Issue under-counted at 7 types/14 sites.)
- **Lowercasing** centralised onto `core/normalization` helpers (`normalize_identifier` / `normalize_ascii_lowercase`) across ~13 files (lockout repos, peer registry, a2a gateway, training controller, provider discovery/allowlist/url/capability, DNS pinning, git/network validators, GitHub health check).
- **`_parse_response`** deduped into `memory/procedural/_response_parsing.py`; both procedural proposers delegate.
- **clip+ellipsis** onto `core/text_clipping.clip_with_ellipsis` (`reformulation.py`, `meta/telemetry/emitter.py`, preserving the 500-char total bound).
- **`PersonalityMode`**: single `engine/_personality_section.py` consumed by both the token estimator and the prompt renderer (replaces the inline Jinja branch).
- **`change_type` validation**: shared `engine/_diff_invariants.py`; the workflow and identity diffs delegate.
- **Backend selection** routed through `persistence/backend_dispatch.build_for_backend` in the conversational / charter / upgrade-recommendation factories.

**Factory / service error-path logging**
- Added structured `logger.warning`/`logger.info` on previously-silent error and state-transition paths across ~12 factory/service modules, with new event constants in `observability/events/{git,pipeline,charter,consolidation,knowledge,timeout,integrations,security,persistence}.py`. The forge-API factory logs only `base_url_scheme` (never the full URL, which can carry credentials).
- The two procedural proposers and the evolution analyzer now pass their already-registered `purpose=` to `cost_recording_scope`, closing grandfathered cost-attribution debt (baseline shrunk accordingly).

**Docstring accuracy**
- Fixed `set_slice` (wire-vs-swap), the timeout scheduler lock-conditional, and `worker.stop()` lock semantics; corrected `_extract_json`, the state-slice write-pattern count, and several review-surfaced docstrings.
- Removed the lint-permitted redundant `Returns:` from the 8 property accessors in `state_per_op_limits.py` / `state_bridge_config.py`.
- `test_gateway.py`: hoisted ~91 in-method imports to module level + module `pytestmark`.

## Scope notes

- **`Returns:` removal is partial by design.** `DOC201` is enforced repo-wide and only exempts `@property` accessors; validators and value-returning functions must keep `Returns:`. So the issue's `_backend_accessors.py` (~152 sections), `_deep_copy_*` validators, cassette, and consolidation-extractor targets are gate-blocked from removal. The 8 removable property sections are done here; the codebase-wide tail (chiefly the two ~1100-line `_backend_accessors.py`) goes to a follow-up issue.
- **Three "logger-less" checklist items were already covered** (`signals.py`, `preset_override_service.py`, `pipeline/factory.py` all already import `get_logger` with full coverage) and were skipped.

## Pre-PR review

17 review agents run; 24 findings implemented (2 Critical, 1 High, 5 Major, plus Medium/Low) and verified. One finding was **reverted after attempting**: unifying the factory guards on `backend.kind` (a Low "consistency" suggestion) broke the shared-app boot, because the test `FakePersistenceBackend` deliberately returns `backend_name="fake"` while `kind=SQLITE` (with an explicit "do not branch on kind for the fake" comment). `backend_name` is the intentional "is this a real usable backend?" discriminator, so the guard stays on it.

Deliberately not changed (reviewed): the lockout repos now use `normalize_identifier` (`strip().casefold()`) instead of `.lower()`. This is a security tightening (closes a whitespace-padded lockout-key bypass) and a Unicode-safe upgrade; for the ASCII usernames this path handles it is value-equivalent.

- Dual-backend filter-clause parity covered by the existing `tests/conformance/persistence/` suite.

pull request introduces significant performance improvements and caching to the shock generation and Kalman filter matrix construction code. The main changes are the addition of fast NumPy-based paths for common shock distributions (normal, t, uniform), and a new caching mechanism for model-constant Kalman matrices, which avoids redundant computation during repeated filtering with unchanged parameters.

**Shock generation improvements:**

* Fast NumPy-based implementations for normal, multivariate normal, t, multivariate t, and uniform shock generators are added, bypassing slower generic SciPy distribution paths for these common cases. This greatly speeds up simulation and estimation workflows. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-31f3b30c0b68ac16ffd3e0510ef3a4a547aabeca1ad0742a9648a465d23aa844R41-R110) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-31f3b30c0b68ac16ffd3e0510ef3a4a547aabeca1ad0742a9648a465d23aa844L56-R128) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-31f3b30c0b68ac16ffd3e0510ef3a4a547aabeca1ad0742a9648a465d23aa844L79-R151) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-31f3b30c0b68ac16ffd3e0510ef3a4a547aabeca1ad0742a9648a465d23aa844L103-R174) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-31f3b30c0b68ac16ffd3e0510ef3a4a547aabeca1ad0742a9648a465d23aa844L127-R198) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-31f3b30c0b68ac16ffd3e0510ef3a4a547aabeca1ad0742a9648a465d23aa844L145-R216)
* The shock generator selection logic was updated to use these fast paths automatically when possible, falling back to the generic path only for less common or custom distributions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-31f3b30c0b68ac16ffd3e0510ef3a4a547aabeca1ad0742a9648a465d23aa844R315-R321) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-31f3b30c0b68ac16ffd3e0510ef3a4a547aabeca1ad0742a9648a465d23aa844R335-R373)

**Kalman filter caching and validation:**

* A new `_KFMatrices` dataclass is introduced to cache model-constant Kalman matrices (`C`, `d`, `Q`, `P0`, and `R_const`) for each unique calibration and filter configuration. This cache is stored on the `SolvedModel` object and keyed by a fingerprint of calibration parameters and other filter options, ensuring correctness when parameters change. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-210374c397e1b2484fef28fd345a2cbe7054b2e03b3b7c0dbf6fb43bf8015f10R29-R49) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4ac494e8a6b5ac8b433896a1c6df329142512a54414629d8189f27459e7e6dadR72-R113) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-210374c397e1b2484fef28fd345a2cbe7054b2e03b3b7c0dbf6fb43bf8015f10R82-R124)
* The Kalman filter interface (`KalmanInterface`) now uses this cache to avoid redundant matrix construction on repeated filter calls with the same configuration, significantly improving performance in Monte Carlo, MLE, and MCMC scenarios.
* Validation of matrix symmetry and non-negative diagonals is now performed only once per cached set of constant matrices, rather than on every filter call, further reducing overhead.

**Testing and compatibility:**

* The Kalman filter interface test stubs are updated to mirror the new caching contract, ensuring that tests exercise the cache-aware construction path.

These changes collectively improve both the speed and correctness of simulation and estimation routines in the codebase.

Summary

- Adds a `sync-plugin-manifest` job to the Publish workflow that runs after `publish` on stable `v*` tag pushes and `workflow_dispatch` triggers. It checks out `main`, sets `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` to the tag version via `sed` (same byte-preserving approach as `just release`), and pushes directly to `main` as `github-actions[bot]`. Prerelease tags and already-matching versions are no-ops. A 3-attempt retry loop handles non-fast-forward races.
- Removes the hard-fail version check in the `publish` job (now informational) and in the `just tag` recipe. Maintainers can run `just tag X.Y.Z` without a prior release-prep PR.
- Updates `CONTRIBUTING.md` to document the new two-step flow (tag, then CI auto-bumps) and the required one-time repo setting.

## REQUIRED one-time repo setting

> **The auto-commit push will fail until this is done.**

A repository administrator must add **`github-actions[bot]`** to the "Allow specified actors to bypass required pull requests" list under **Settings > Branches > main** branch protection rules. Required status checks must also not block the bot's direct push.

Without this setting, the `sync-plugin-manifest` job will fail to push and `plugin.json` on `main` will remain at its previous value (the release itself - PyPI publish and GitHub Release - is unaffected).

## Test plan

- The push-to-main path only runs on a real stable tag; it cannot be exercised by PR CI. The logic has been reviewed for correctness:
  - Prerelease-skip regex matches the existing pattern used throughout the workflow.
  - `git diff --quiet` guards against empty commits.
  - Injection safety: `EFFECTIVE_TAG` is injected via `env:` (not `${{ }}` in the script body), matching the existing pattern.
  - YAML syntax validated with `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(...))"`.
- The first real stable tag after merging this PR will be the end-to-end validation.

Closes #912

Replace `httpx.AsyncClient` with `curl_cffi.AsyncSession(impersonate="chrome131")` across all three scraper fetch files. `curl_cffi` bundles `libcurl-impersonate-chrome` (compiled against BoringSSL with Chrome's exact TLS fingerprint), allowing Tiers 1-2 to bypass CDN-level bot detection that currently blocks at TLS handshake time.

**Proof of concept** — same Akamai-protected NDTV page:

| Client | Status | Latency |
|--------|--------|---------|
| `httpx.AsyncClient` (current) | 403 | 0.1s |
| `curl_cffi.AsyncSession(impersonate="chrome131")` | **200** | **0.7s** |

Summary

Fixes #248. Hardens the local transfer service with a DB-backed single-use confirmation token, service-layer ownership and precision enforcement, deadlock-safe row locking, tamper-evident transaction hashes, and redacted audit metadata. Adds 27 new security tests.

## Why

The previous implementation had six exploitable gaps:

- **Concurrent double-submit**: `session.pop` anti-replay was insufficient against concurrent confirm requests; an attacker could race two requests through before either consumed the session key
- **Payee ownership bypass**: ownership was only checked at the route layer; a direct service call or future refactor could skip it
- **Fractional-cent injection**: decimal precision was not validated in the service, so a client could submit amounts like `10.001` if they bypassed WTForms validation
- **Deadlock risk**: row locking order was not guaranteed in SQL, so concurrent transfers between the same two accounts could deadlock
- **Audit data exposure (OWASP A09)**: raw transfer references appeared in the security audit log
- **No tamper detection**: no cryptographic record existed to detect post-insert alteration of transaction rows

## What changed

### `app/models.py`
- Added `PendingTransfer` model (`token`, `user_id`, `payee_id`, `amount`, `reference`, `expires_at`, `consumed_at`, `consumed_transaction_ref`, `created_at`)
- `PendingTransfer.amount` uses `Numeric(12, 5)` scale so sub-cent amounts survive the SQLite float round-trip for service-layer precision enforcement
- Added `transaction_hash` column to `Transaction` (SHA-256 of ref + sender + recipient + amount + reference + created_at, unique index)
- Added `ck_users_balance_non_negative` CHECK and `ck_transactions_amount_positive` CHECK (PostgreSQL only; see migration note)

### `migrations/versions/20260628_0016_harden_local_transfer.py`
- Creates `pending_transfers` table with token unique index and expiry index
- Adds `transaction_hash` column with unique index to `transactions`
- Adds CHECK constraints via `ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT` for PostgreSQL only â€” `batch_alter_table` cannot reflect table schema in Alembic offline (`--sql`) mode, so the constraints are skipped for SQLite where application-layer validation is the enforcement mechanism

### `app/banking/services.py`
- `execute_local_transfer` now accepts `confirmation_token` (not raw amount/reference); all financial data is read from the `PendingTransfer` DB record
- Enforces payee ownership and cooldown at the service layer independently of the route
- Rejects self-transfers and unavailable recipient accounts
- Precision check: `Decimal(str(amount)).normalize()` strips trailing zeros from the wider `Numeric(12,5)` scale before the `exponent < -2` guard, so `10.001` is correctly rejected while `10.10` (stored as `10.10000`) passes
- Atomically consumes `PendingTransfer` with `SELECT FOR UPDATE`; second concurrent confirm gets 409
- Locks user rows with `ORDER BY id ASC` before `SELECT FOR UPDATE` (deadlock prevention)
- Computes and stores `transaction_hash` before insert
- Replaces raw reference in audit metadata with `reference_present` / `reference_length` (OWASP A09)

### `app/banking/routes.py`
- `transfer_submit`: creates a `PendingTransfer` DB record; stores only the opaque token in session
- `transfer_confirm`: reads token from session, fetches `PendingTransfer` from DB
- `transfer_confirm_submit`: pops token from session, passes it to the service

### `tests/test_local_transfer.py`
- Added `_make_pending_transfer` helper; updated four direct-service tests to supply confirmation tokens

### `tests/test_local_transfer_security.py`
- 27 new tests covering: payee ownership, self-transfer, recipient state policy, decimal precision, anti-replay, token binding, locking query ORDER BY, audit redaction, cooldown enforcement, atomicity, transaction_hash presence and sensitivity, consumed token bookkeeping
- `test_service_rejects_payee_in_cooldown`: uses a fresh user `carol` (account `901000099`) to avoid unique constraint collision with the existing aliceâ†’bob payee in `sec_ctx`

### `tests/conftest.py`
- Added `test_local_transfer_security.py` to `SECURITY_TEST_FILES`

## Security impact

| Gap | Fix |
|---|---|
| Concurrent double-submit replay | DB-backed atomic token with `SELECT FOR UPDATE`; second confirm gets 409 |
| Payee ownership bypass | Enforced in service layer independently of routes |
| Fractional-cent injection | `normalize()` + `exponent < -2` guard in service; `Numeric(12,5)` preserves sub-cent amounts through DB round-trip |
| Deadlock risk | Guaranteed `ORDER BY id ASC` before `SELECT FOR UPDATE` |
| Audit PII exposure (OWASP A09) | Reference replaced with `reference_present` + `reference_length` |
| Post-insert tampering | SHA-256 `transaction_hash` covers all financial fields |

## Deployment impact

Requires migration `20260628_0016` before deploying:
- Creates `pending_transfers` table
- Adds `transaction_hash` column with unique index to `transactions`
- Adds CHECK constraints to `users` and `transactions` (PostgreSQL only)

No EC2 bootstrap changes, secret changes, or staging-only steps required. Users who have a pending transfer in session at the moment of deploy will be redirected to the payees page to start a fresh transfer.

## Verification

1. Run `pytest tests/test_local_transfer.py tests/test_local_transfer_security.py` â€” all tests pass
2. Complete a transfer end-to-end: submit amount + MFA, confirm, verify success flash and correct balances
3. Query `transactions` after a transfer: `transaction_hash` must be a 64-character hex string
4. Check `SecurityAuditEvent` for the transfer: `reference` key must not appear; `reference_present` and `reference_length` must be present
5. Submit the confirm form twice with the same token: second attempt must return 409

Summary

- Created `PlannerRole`, a new built-in agent role that analyzes project state and proposes tasks without requiring an existing issue number
- Added `PlannedTask` Pydantic model with 7 fields (title, description, priority, complexity, component, rationale, dependencies) for structured task proposals
- Registered the role in the dispatcher and added comprehensive test coverage

## Changes

**Core Implementation** (`sova/roles/planner.py`):
- `PlannedTask` model: structured representation of proposed tasks with priority, complexity, component area, rationale, and dependency tracking
- `PlannerRole` class: implements `AgentRole` ABC with `allowed_input_states=frozenset()` and `output_state=None` to support issueless operation
- Context gathering: reads open issues, VISION.md content, recent PRs, and project config to inform planning
- LLM invocation: uses direct `invoke()` call with structured prompt requesting JSON array of proposals
- Robust parsing: handles malformed JSON, markdown fencing, and empty responses with graceful fallbacks
- Dual handoff persistence: writes both file-based `DashboardHandoff` (for dashboard UI) and DB-backed `AgentHandoff` (for history)

**Registration** (`sova/roles/dispatcher.py`, `sova/roles/__init__.py`):
- Added `PlannerRole` to `_ROLES` dict for explicit role invocation
- Exported from roles module for external use

**Tests** (`tests/test_roles.py`):
- Metadata validation (name, input states, output state)
- Execute happy path with mocked LLM returning valid task proposals
- LLM failure handling (parse errors, empty responses)
- Dispatcher integration with issueless context
- Edge cases: missing VISION.md, adapter failures, None task_run_id

**Documentation** (`AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/architecture.md`):
- Updated role counts from 5→6 built-in roles

## Review Guidance

- **LLM prompt structure**: verify the prompt provides sufficient context for quality proposals while staying under token budgets
- **JSON parsing robustness**: check fallback paths handle all malformed response cases (extra fencing, partial JSON, wrong schema)
- **Issueless validation**: confirm `validate_preconditions()` override and empty `allowed_input_states` correctly bypass issue-based checks
- **Handoff writing**: verify the `if ctx.task_run_id` guard prevents DB write failures in CLI-direct invocations
- **Test coverage**: ensure mocked LLM responses match real Claude output structure

## Test Plan

- All existing tests pass (`make check` ✓)
- New `TestPlannerRole` class covers:
  - Metadata validation (name, states, output)
  - Execute with valid LLM response → success, findings populated, handoffs written
  - Execute with LLM parse failure → `RoleResult(success=False)`, no exception
  - Execute with missing VISION.md → proceeds with empty vision context
  - Execute with adapter list_tasks failure → proceeds with empty issue list
  - Dispatcher `get_role("planner")` returns `PlannerRole` instance
  - Dispatcher handles issueless context with explicit `--role planner`
- Manual verification: spawned a planner run via `sova run --role planner` (requires #166 for full dashboard integration)

Closes #310

## Purpose

**Make a brownfield arrival augment a project's existing branch-protection rule in place, instead of standing up a second engine-named rule alongside it.**

- The locked design ("CODEOWNERS and the ruleset", provisioning README L498–507) wants one augmented ruleset, not two: read the project's rule, merge the engine's required-check names into it, write the union; on clean removal, take back only what was added — "augmented, never weakened."
- This was the highest-consequence write in the brownfield arrival (it mutates live branch protection), deliberately split out of slice 6b (#234) for undistracted review and tracked as #310.

*<Impact: completes the brownfield arrival path — a project that already protects its main branch keeps one coherent rule, with the engine's checks added to it, rather than two overlapping rules.>*

## Scope

**The in-place augment + a symmetric de-bootstrap, recorded so removal reverses exactly what arrival added.**

- `bootstrap.py`: a fail-closed read-modify-write — `product_rulesets` (which rulesets actually bite on the branch, via the evaluated endpoint's `ruleset_id`), `ruleset_detail` (the full object the list endpoint omits), and a pure `augment_payload` that whitelist-projects to the writable fields, unions the engine's checks, and adds any wholly-missing floor rule type. The write is verified against the re-read ruleset object (immediately consistent), with a post-write byte-identical preservation check that fails closed, a bounded re-read on a concurrent overwrite, and a defined degraded terminal state.
- `apply()` chooses repair-own / augment-one-product / create-own (+ disclosure when more than one rule, or protection is via classic branch protection); `de_bootstrap()` reverses exactly the recorded additions and never deletes a product rule.
- The exact additions are persisted in `engine.json` (`control_plane` marker, with a schema entry) by the control-plane apply step; `module_manager.remove_engine` reads it back and the removal PR body discloses the augmented-removal case.
- New operator copy for every outcome (augment, partial-floor, ambiguity, classic-coexistence, augmented-removal); a behavioral demo (`instantiator augment-demo`) and demo Part N in the removal demo; tests across all three tools.

*<Impact: a brownfield project's own protection is strengthened, never altered, and the engine can be removed cleanly leaving the project's rule exactly as it was.>*

## Out of scope

**Anything that would change a setting the operator chose, or write to systems the spec does not cover.**

- The engine never modifies an *existing* product rule's parameters (e.g. a PR rule that allows unresolved-comment merges) — that gap is disclosed in plain language, not rewritten.
- Classic branch protection is not written to: where a project protects main that way (no ruleset to augment), the engine creates its own ruleset and the systems compose; the coexistence is disclosed.
- More than one product rule covering main → the engine does not guess which to augment; it creates its own and says so.

*<Impact: the engine's footprint on someone else's live protection stays additive and predictable; ambiguous or out-of-model cases fall back to the known-safe behavior with disclosure.>*

## Risk

**Guardrail-weakening: this edits guarded `.engine/tools/` files (`engine-guard` will flag the PR for the maintainer's `guardrail-ack`). The change writes to live branch protection, so "never weaken the operator's rule" is the load-bearing invariant.**

- A wholesale-replace PUT could, in principle, drop a product rule/check/bypass. Mitigated by: a whitelist projection (never a verbatim echo of the GET's read-only fields), preservation of `bypass_actors`/`conditions` verbatim, and a post-write re-read that asserts every product rule is byte-identical and fails closed otherwise.
- Removal could weaken protection by stripping a check the engine didn't add. Mitigated by the recorded marker (reverse exactly the added set); the marker-absent fallback strips only the two frozen engine check names (bounded, never deletes a product rule).
- A concurrent edit in the read-write window: bounded re-read + retry, then a degraded terminal state — never a false "applied".

*<Impact: the never-weaken guarantee rests on a runtime check, not an assertion; the worst case degrades and discloses rather than silently altering protection.>*

## Validation

**Mechanical green on the rebased base: the validator suite, the full test suite, and every control-plane demo.**

- `validate.py` suite 'CI': passed, no hard findings (knowledge-coverage, operation-shape, coherence, first-run-reference-closure all green; only the pre-existing soft "not active here / runs in CI" notes remain).
- `python -m unittest discover -s tools`: 2445 tests pass, run against the worktree. New coverage: `augment_payload` (additive, read-only-field stripping, residual disclosure), apply-augments (no second rule, preservation, partial, retry, fail-closed-on-partial-read, ambiguity/classic fallbacks, server-drops-an-added-rule → degraded, normalization tolerated, param-change caught), de-bootstrap augmented + marker-absent fallback, the `engine.json` marker persist, and the demo-green tests.
- Demos: `instantiator augment-demo` and the removal demo's new Part N both pass — each captures the operator's rule before/after and asserts it is byte-identical except the engine's additions.

*<Impact: an approver can rely on the additive-and-reversible behavior being exercised by tests and demonstrably falsifiable, not just described.>*

## Review

**Two cold review rounds ran (plan gate before the build, deliverable gate after); each blocking and serious finding was fixed and the fixes were validated but not re-reviewed, so the reviewed version and the merged version differ.**

- Plan gate (four independent cold lenses: architecture, feasibility, product-intent, risk-governance) ground-truthed the plan against source and the GitHub rulesets API; its findings shaped the build (whitelist projection + preservation check, the recorded marker for an exact inverse, object-read verification with a degraded terminal state) and one product fork was escalated to the maintainer (augment "strengthens to the floor" by addition only, disclosing what can't be added).
- Deliverable gate (four independent cold lenses: spec-conformance, technical-integrity, security-governance, usability) reviewed the built change. It found 1 blocking + 3 serious + nits, all fixed in this PR: the augment now verifies the floor against the re-read object (a server that drops an added rule degrades + discloses rather than falsely reporting protection on); the preservation check tolerates GitHub's parameter normalization by sub-mapping while still catching any operator-owned drop/change; the template-drift test actually catches a dropped section; and the partial-floor disclosure now states the consequence + how to act. Each step completed; spec-conformance and usability reported no blocking/serious. The post-review fixes were validated (full suite + demos green) but not put back through the cold lenses.
- Inductive ceiling, named in the demo and not dischargeable by a fixture: a live GET→PUT round-trip of a real adopter's populated ruleset. The API facts relied on were verified against GitHub's documented rulesets API (list omits rules; PUT replaces wholesale with no If-Match; `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` literal); a live admin write was not run in this environment.

*<Impact: the engine's own account of the review — the maintainer's merge is the binding gate.>*

## Files of interest

**The augment logic and its safety checks.**

- `.engine/tools/bootstrap.py` — `augment_payload` / `_project_ruleset` / `_product_preserved` / `_augment_ruleset` / `de_bootstrap` (the read-modify-write and its inverse).
- `.engine/tools/instantiator.py` — `_persist_control_plane_marker` (records the marker) and `augment_demo`.
- `.engine/tools/module_manager.py` — the marker read + the augmented-removal PR-body branch + demo Part N.
- `.engine/schemas/engine.v1.json` — the `control_plane` marker shape.

*<Impact: these determine whether the augment is genuinely additive and exactly reversible.>*

## Claude involvement

**Design decisions are recorded; the edits are mechanical against them.**

- Maintainer decision (recorded this session via the question surface): augment "strengthens to the floor" by addition only. Build-spec leaves decided and recorded in the plan: the stateless-vs-marker choice (reversed to a recorded marker for an exact inverse), the whitelist projection, the object-read verification, the >1-rule and classic-protection fallbacks.
- AI judgment is load-bearing in the safety design (preservation check, fail-closed reads, bounded retry); the rest is mechanical wiring and copy.

*<Impact: where AI judgment matters most here is the never-weaken safety envelope, which is verified by tests and the byte-identical demo rather than taken on trust.>*

Summary

Closes #347.

Implements the M4 HELD2 Stage II electrolyte dual phase-discovery slice for the public native/package validation route. The `_native_electrolyte_held2_phase_discovery` path now consumes the continuous reduced-electroneutral Stage I certificate, constructs a material-balance complement candidate for accepted negative TPD cuts, reruns candidate selection, and emits the shared Stage II bound/replay diagnostics.

This PR does not claim Stage III refinement, postsolve certification, or public electrolyte route admission. Those remain separate HELD2 path issues.

## Retained evidence

- Stage II status: `dual_loop_verified`; bound audit: `candidate_bound_gap_closed`; dual loop: `verified`.
- Bounds: lower `-0.36067618496483983`, upper `-0.36067618496483983`, gap `0.0`, tolerance `1e-08`, candidate count `5`, selected count `2`.
- Replay payload: fractions `[0.08980929801532778, 0.9101907019846722]`, max charge residual `0.0`, max composition-sum residual `0.0`, Stage III status `pending_ipopt_refinement`.
- Rejected candidates: ranks `[0, 2, 3]`, all with `not_selected_by_dual_loop_mass_balance_gate` plus retained TPD, charge, composition, and domain diagnostics.
- Reduced-basis coverage: neutral-only, Khudaida single-salt NaCl, Ascani common-ion, and Ascani mixed-salt fixtures; max charge residual `3.47e-18`, max round-trip residual `2.43e-18`.

Summary

ADR-0001/0016 cleanup from the #1328 player-reachability audit. The web `FashionPresentationViewSet` reached the present-outfit capability through `FashionPresentationSerializer.create()` calling `present_outfit` **directly**, bypassing the **registered** `PresentOutfitAction`. Two web paths for one capability — and the web path skipped the Action's trigger events + scene message that telnet fires.

## What changed

- **`FashionPresentationViewSet.create()`** now dispatches `PresentOutfitAction.run()`. The serializer stays as the **I/O contract** — it validates `event`/`outfit` input and serializes the result — but no longer orchestrates. Its `create()` bypass is removed.
- **`PresentOutfitAction.execute`** now returns the created `FashionPresentation` in `result.data["presentation"]`, so the viewset serializes the response without a re-query (telnet ignores it).
- **Web parity gain:** the web POST now also emits `BEFORE_PRESENT_OUTFIT` / `PRESENT_OUTFIT` and the "…presents your look" scene message, matching telnet.

This is the conclusion from the design discussion: converging loses **nothing** — the serializer's valuable parts (PK validation, response serialization, OpenAPI schema → api-types) all stay; only the anti-pattern (business logic in `serializer.create()`) is retired.

## Schema / drift

The serializer's `fields` are unchanged, so the request/response **shape** is identical. The schema regen touches only the operation/serializer **description** text (the new docstrings) — committed. No frontend component change (nothing rendered the bypass differently).

## Tests

- Adds `test_present_endpoint_dispatches_present_outfit_action` — spies the real `run` (it still executes → 201) and asserts the endpoint took the Action path, so a regression back to the serializer bypass fails.
- Existing `test_fashion_api` POST/400/auth cases pass unchanged against the converged endpoint.

## Testing

`ruff` + `ty` clean (the pre-existing `fashion.py` ty notes on `intent_event`/`initialize_state_for_object` are untouched). `world.items.tests.test_fashion_api` 9/9; full `actions` suite (759) + ceremony/momentum green.

Closes #1508.

Summary

Hardens the GUI against malformed input surfaced by the authorised end-to-end robustness test (2026-06-28). A single anti-pattern (raw `request.GET`/`POST` values fed straight into typed ORM filters) made dozens of endpoints return HTTP 500 on a bad UUID/int/date, the advanced filter and global search had their own crash/DoS paths, and a handful of other entry points (incl. the dashboard WebSocket) raised unhandled exceptions. All are now validated/coerced so bad input degrades gracefully, never a 500. One commit per issue.

`#157` was already merged on `main` (commit `b3d8d62`), so it is not part of this PR.

- **#154** : new shared `core.query_params` helper (`parse_uuid` / `parse_int` / `parse_date_param`) coercing untrusted values before the ORM. Applied to the risk register (list, table-body, bulk action, Excel export), treatments, acceptances, threats, vulnerabilities, ISO 27005, scale-choices, parent-assessment lookups; compliance requirements (`?framework=`) and assessment-result create (`?requirement=`); suppliers (`?supplier_type=`, integer PK bounded); and the calendar feed (`?start=` / `?end=`).

## Problem

`read_file_metadata` opened the whole h5ad via `anndata.read_h5ad(path, backed="r")` just to read `obs` + `uns`. anndata's backed mode is **X-only** — `read_h5ad_backed` (anndata `_io/h5ad.py`) eagerly `read_elem`s `layers` and `raw`. On files with multi-billion-nonzero matrices, that open spiked to **15–24+ GB (nondeterministic)** and OOM-killed the 60 GB Batch container *mid-metadata-read*. Prod symptom: `integrated_all_tissues_object.h5ad` stuck "pending" (job `5cbae667`, exit 137, "container killed due to memory usage").

The investigation showed the validators themselves are **not** the problem.

## Measured peak RSS on the offending file (2.24M × 36.6k; X/raw.X/`ambient_corrected` each ~7.6B nnz = 256 GB if fully resident)

| step | peak RSS | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| CAP validator | 2.71 GB | ✅ completes |
| HCA schema validator (dask-chunked) | 15.42 GB | ✅ completes (26 min) |
| **metadata `read_h5ad(backed="r")`** | **15 → 24+ GB** | ❌ nondeterministic, OOMs |
| **metadata via `read_elem` (this PR)** | **1.37 GB** | ✅ |

## Change

- `read_file_metadata` now reads `obs` + `uns` via targeted `read_elem` and gets shape from the X header — never opening X/raw/layers. Summary + coverage are unchanged (they only need obs/uns; `read_elem(obs)` is anndata's own obs-read path, so output is identical).
- New `matrix_storage` payload field: per-matrix/layer `format, n_obs, n_vars, nnz, data_dtype, index_dtype, on_disk_bytes, resident_bytes`, from a new pure-h5py `hca_validation.h5ad_storage` module (HDF5 header only, no matrix load). Additive + SNS-safe — the tracker's Yup schema ignores unknown keys (persistence tracked in clevercanary/hca-atlas-tracker#1436).
- `h5py` wired as an optional `h5ad` extra on `shared` so the entry-sheet Lambda stays lean.

## Tests

- Swapped the now-bypassed `read_h5ad` mock for a mockable read seam (`_read_metadata_inputs`/`get_matrix_storage`).
- Added `test_read_file_metadata_real_h5ad` exercising the real (unmocked) read path end-to-end.
- New `shared/tests/test_h5ad_storage.py` (incl. the int32-vs-int64 index footprint case).
- Full suite green (28 dataset-validator + 4 shared); pyright clean on changed files.

## Notes

- This **supersedes** the EC2/512 GB direction in clevercanary/hca-atlas-tracker-tf-config#68 — nothing in the pipeline needs >~15 GB once this lands.
- Follow-up #448: reuse the shared helper in `hca-anndata-tools/storage.py` + fix the same backed-read OOM in `get_summary`.

Summary

`provider: auto` with a local `base_url` (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, …) now routes to that endpoint instead of silently sending the request to a cloud API. Fixes #3846.

**Root cause:** `resolve_provider("auto")` scans environment variables and returns a cloud provider (e.g. `anthropic` when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set) *before* `config.model.base_url` is ever consulted. A user on local Ollama got `HTTP 401` / "credit balance too low" because their request went to `https://api.anthropic.com`, ignoring `base_url: http://localhost:11434`.

## Changes

- `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py`: in `resolve_runtime_provider()`, before calling `resolve_provider()`, short-circuit to the OpenAI-compatible resolver when no explicit creds were passed, `provider` is `auto`/unset, and a non-cloud `base_url` is configured. Well-known cloud roots (`openrouter.ai`, `anthropic.com`, `openai.com`) are matched on **host** (via `base_url_host_matches`), not substring — so a look-alike host (`api.anthropic.com.attacker.test`) can't evade the bypass and leak a cloud credential.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_runtime_provider_resolution.py`: 3 tests — the #3846 regression, cloud base_url still routes to anthropic (no regression), and the look-alike-host guard.

## Validation

| Config (`provider: auto`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `base_url: http://localhost:11434` | → `api.anthropic.com` (401) | → `localhost:11434` ✓ |
| `base_url: https://api.anthropic.com` | → anthropic | → anthropic ✓ |
| `base_url: http://api.anthropic.com.attacker.test/v1` | → anthropic (leak) | → custom ✓ |

135 tests passing in `tests/hermes_cli/test_runtime_provider_resolution.py` (132 existing + 3 new). Verified end-to-end with the reported config against a temp `HERMES_HOME`.

Salvages @Mibayy's PR #3997; cherry-picked onto current `main` with authorship preserved, host-match hardening + test relocation added on top.

- Replaces provider-localized titles (e.g. "Encuentros en la tercera fase") with the TMDb `en-US` canonical title ("Close Encounters of the Third Kind") for all enriched movies
- Populates `original_lang` from TMDb `original_language` during enrichment
- Adds `_filter_english` in `pipeline.py` to drop movies with a confirmed non-English `original_lang` after enrichment, blocking cases like "El drama" (Mexican Spanish-language film) from appearing in results

Title-based cache lookup breaks when the scraper title differs from the TMDb English title — the `_find_cached_movie` lookup uses the fresh scraper title as the key, but the cache is now indexed by TMDb titles. v0.10.0 — Live Notepad + Knowledge Adapters

Last feature sprint before 1.0. Steer summaries with live notes, and decouple export behind a pluggable adapter. Sprint mode: **HOLD**.

### Commits (bisectable, dependency-first)

| Commit | Scope |
|---|---|
| `feat(config)` | `[knowledge_store]` config + provider validation (#54) |
| `feat(database)` | `user_notes` column + idempotent migration (#53) |
| `feat(knowledge)` | `KnowledgeStore` port + `local-markdown` adapter (#54) |
| `feat(session)` | inject `user_notes` into summaries + wire export (#53, #54) |
| `feat(server)` | `user_notes` endpoints; regenerate honors notes (#53) |
| `feat(ui)` | live notepad panel (#53) |
| `test` | notepad + knowledge-adapter coverage |
| `chore(release)` | v0.10.0 bump + lockfile + docs + gitignore `.claude/` |

### What shipped

- **Live Notepad (#53)** — notepad `<textarea>` captures notes during a recording; `user_notes` persisted per session and injected into the AI summary via a `{user_notes}` placeholder (back-compat fallback prepends them when a custom prompt omits it). Honored on stop, saved-session re-generation, **and** live generation. Capture-during, inject-at-generation.

**Motivation.** When the agentic `/chat` path is enabled, every question — including off-domain ones — enters the deep-agent loop, spending model and tool calls on queries the assistant is not meant to answer. This adds Wave A / A3: an agricultural intent filter that deflects off-domain questions before the loop. Closes #172.

**Task Link.** https://github.com/LukeSantossz/sb100_agents/issues/172

**Spec Link.** [`SPEC.md` @ 068f88b](https://github.com/LukeSantossz/sb100_agents/blob/068f88b/SPEC.md) — ephemeral; it is removed as the final commit before merge. Durable rationale promoted to [ADR-0010](https://github.com/LukeSantossz/sb100_agents/blob/feat/172-agricultural-intent-filter/docs/adr/0010-domain-gate-retrieval-score.md), indexed by the README Engineering Decisions section.

## What Was Done

- `core/config.py`: `intent_filter_enabled` (default `True`) and `intent_threshold` (default `0.3`, validated `0.0..1.0`).
- `retrieval/vector_store.py`: `top_similarity(embedding) -> float | None` (top-1 Qdrant search); exported from `retrieval`. `search_context` unchanged.
- `agent/intent.py`: `classify_domain`, the `DomainDecision` dataclass, and the user-facing `OUT_OF_DOMAIN_MESSAGE` (pt-BR). Embeds the question and compares the top corpus similarity to `intent_threshold`; **fails open** (in-domain + structured log) on any embedding/search error or an empty result.
- `api/routes/chat.py`: in the agent branch, before `invoke_agent`, gate on `classify_domain` when `intent_filter_enabled`; emit a structured `chat.intent` log (`username`, `in_domain`, `score`, `threshold`); off-domain returns `OUT_OF_DOMAIN_MESSAGE` with `hallucination_score=0.0`, records the turn in the conversation buffer, and skips the loop. The legacy (non-agent) path is unchanged.
- `docs/adr/0010-domain-gate-retrieval-score.md` + a README Engineering Decisions row.
- Tests: settings validation, `top_similarity`, `classify_domain` (incl. both fail-open paths), and `/chat` route gating (short-circuit, pass-through, filter-disabled bypass, structured-log); pre-existing agent-path tests kept hermetic.

The corpus is the domain reference (a coverage proxy for "agricultural intent"), so the gate scales with ingestion and needs no labels; a few-shot topic classifier is the documented escalation if measurement shows topic leakage or over-blocking. The gate is dormant until `agent_enabled` is turned on.

First implementation step of **Track B** in epic #210 (intermediate products & cloud-as-source-of-truth).

## What this does

Adds a `deploy_status` lifecycle and threads a **fail-closed published predicate through every reader**, so that when B2 (#218) starts deploying `in_prep` intermediate products, none of them reach non-admins. **B1 ships everything `published` → zero user-visible change.** It is the safety prerequisite that B2's `deploy --in-prep` capability-gates on.

**Readers only.** `has_published_spectrum` is always `true` in B1 (nothing is `in_prep`), so every predicate added here is a no-op until B2 — the point is that readers are status-aware *before* `in_prep` data exists. Population/recompute logic and the deploy write-path are B2. No `python/campfire` changes, no `pipeline/**` (so no CHANGELOG entry).

## Schema (`supabase/schemas/` + `20260629014642_add_deploy_status_lifecycle.sql`)

- `spectra.deploy_status` (`in_prep|published|revoked`, default `published`, CHECK) + `targets`/`objects.has_published_spectrum` (default `true`) — all fail-closed-visible. Partial index on the rare non-published case (the published-path covering index is deferred to B2, where real `in_prep` volume can drive an EXPLAIN).
- **RLS**: every science reader gated — `spectra` (primary), `targets`/`objects`/`object_photometry`/`object_list_members`, `comments` + `flag_audit_log` (all branches), the 3 inspector-UPDATE policies, and `shutters`/`slit_regions` via a zero-change `NOT EXISTS` form.
- **RPCs** (`functions.sql`): 17 readers threaded with `p_include_unpublished` (admin opt-in, `DEFAULT false`) + the predicate — including 3-CTE consistency on the `*_for_sync` RPCs (so totals match the row set) and `object_scoped_aggregates()` threaded into its 3 callers. Admin opt-in derives **only** from `is_admin()`, never from program slugs.
- **Views**: `mv_filter_options`/`mv_programs_overview` published-filtered; `spectrum_flag_summary` + `nircam_reduction_progress` flipped to `security_invoker` (the latter was leaking NIRCam QA aggregates to all authenticated users — a pre-existing leak).

## Web (17 files)

New `isAdminUser()` helper (explicit `user_profiles.is_admin` lookup via the service-role client, the presign-route pattern). RPC-calling `/api/v1` routes thread `p_include_unpublished`; the direct-read routes that bypass RLS filter `deploy_status='published'` unless admin — critically `/api/v1/spectra` (presign by path), `/spectrum`, and `/redshift-fit`. `og-image` 404s for entities with no published spectrum.

## Why both RLS *and* RPC predicates

The filter RPCs are `SECURITY INVOKER` (verified), so RLS covers user-client reads and the non-`/v1` web routes that never call an RPC. But the same RPCs are also invoked under the service-role key from `/api/v1/*` where RLS is bypassed — so the in-body predicate is also required. Neither layer alone is sufficient.
